page: Amazon Web Services c6id.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 118 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in single-core metrics, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1879.79 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1607.0. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression at 27.91 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 10.3 GB/sec also fall into the average range. However, multi-core and memory-intensive benchmarks are relatively weak. The stress-ng multi-core performance of 1923.38 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1852.0 are rated as poor, reflecting the limitations of its single physical core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read and write speeds of approximately 14.19 GB/sec and 13.42 GB/sec respectively.

The c6id.large offers a qualitative balance of dedicated compute power and high-speed local storage via its bundled 118 GB NVMe SSD, making it a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring fast temporary storage without the overhead of network-attached volumes. However, the low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and poor multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. It is best suited for single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and development environments rather than heavy multi-threaded databases, complex compiling, or large-scale data processing.
